output.summary: Core Rules defines the authoritative Default Game: four Eras, three simultaneous action-selection cycles per Era, and immediate public Mandate scoring. As Seat 2/Kestralyn, I use Kestralyn’s printed faction-board starting values, Mandate, limits, and abilities; this document does not provide those faction-specific details. My infrastructure-compounder path centers on legal Facility placement, local Power, Generator timing, Grid-Ready status, Mega-Clusters, and keeping Facilities powered at game end. Advanced Play, Tactics, secret objectives, and Reserve Specialists are excluded.
keyRules: Use only Default-eligible Headlines without an Advanced Play badge. Do not import any ◆ changes from Advanced Play.

Setup uses a fixed thirteen-tile board: Frontier in the center, a shuffled six-tile operational ring, and a shuffled six-tile public ring. The Map reference supplies the exact pools, positions, adjacency, spaces, and tile effects.
Each Era has its own shuffled Headline deck and three-card Mandate deck. Use three Headlines per Era; reveal one Mandate and return the other two unseen.

My Kestralyn set contains its board, six Core Actions, seven Escalations, CEO, three Teams, four double-sided Facilities, one ordinary Generator, Declare AGI card, track markers, ten Scrutiny cubes, and printed starting resources.
Place my CEO and one Team at Frontier; keep two Teams in supply. Set all tracks and already-earned Mandate to Kestralyn’s printed values. All Scrutiny begins outside the empty Audit bag.
Add every faction’s printed starting Trust and record it as Setup Collective Trust for the final World Ending calculation.
Initiative is chosen randomly. It determines resolution order and unresolved ties, passes clockwise after every action cycle, and cannot be traded or retained.

Each player has six Core Actions—Fund, Research, Build, Organize, Deploy, and Influence—but normally selects only three per Era. A played Core Action stays exhausted until the next Era unless an effect readies it.

Each ordinary cycle is Headline → secret selection → simultaneous reveal → clockwise resolution from Initiative → pass Initiative. During resolution, select is already committed, then move one acting CEO or Team zero to two adjacent hexes, then resolve the chosen card from the destination.

Selection commits only the Action. Piece, path, mode, target, payment, and an immediate trade are chosen during resolution. A selected Action cannot be replaced if it becomes blocked; movement still happens and the Action exhausts without compensation.

Only CEOs and Teams act. A CEO supplies two presence and a Team one. Facilities and Generators never act, although their positions affect construction, Research, Deploy, Influence, Power, production, presence, and control.

An ordinary turn may apply the Action, one destination bonus, one faction modifier, and each applicable global effect. Readying an Action resolves nothing immediately. Agent Swarm is the only compound-Action exception in Default Game order of precedence stated here—but actual card and faction text remains authoritative for named modifications and timing windows: Era unlocks, faction board, Headline, then applicable turn effects/timing exceptions are applied as specified by this rules document and printed components. Systems are inactive until introduced by an Era card’s New this Era strip. Later Eras retain earlier systems unless text says otherwise. All faction abilities, Era cards, and Escalations are open information. Escalation availability is spent to select an unlocked Escalation instead of a Core Action, and unspent availability expires at Era end. Each named Escalation is once per player per game; unused unlocked Escalations remain available later. Era I gives none; Era II gives one and unlocks Mega-Cluster/Reorganization; Era III gives one and unlocks Open Weights/Narrative Capture; Era IV gives two and unlocks Agent Swarm/Declare AGI/Fusion Demonstrator. Runway pays for construction, hiring, partnerships, lobbying, and crises. Compute pays for Research, Deploy, and infrastructure. Capability is permanent model quality and is spent only when instructed. Caps apply immediately after every gain or trade: Runway 12, Compute 10, Safety 3 unless Kestralyn has a printed exception. Excess is returned, and trades cannot route resources through an over-cap state. Cost modifiers apply as replacements/waivers, then surcharges, then discounts; costs cannot fall below zero. Customers produce one Runway each during Production. Customers 1–3 immediately score two Mandate each; Customers 4–5 score one each. Trust ranges from zero to six; reaching Trust 2, 4, and 6 for the first time scores two Mandate at each threshold. Capability normally scores two Mandate the first time it reaches 3, 6, 9, and 12, unless Kestralyn’s printed faction rule changes this. Threshold awards remain earned after later losses. Mandate is scored immediately on the public track. Facilities, controlled hexes, stored resources, and unused cards have no hidden conversion. At setup, printed faction Mandate is awarded only once. The shuffled board remains fixed for all four Eras. A movement step crosses a shared tile edge. Rival pieces may coexist; there is no combat or player elimination. Default Game uses local Power rather than a network. The basic starting grid supplies exactly one dedicated Power to my assigned first Facility, cannot be sold, and cannot satisfy Mega-Cluster’s added demand. Each ordinary Generator supplies only Facilities on its own or adjacent hexes. Facilities do not relay Power. Recalculate eligibility whenever infrastructure moves. Each Facility needs one Power to produce. Mega-Cluster requires its powered hosts plus two additional Power. Power is capacity for one Production only, is never stored, and each unit may be allocated once to a legal recipient. An offline Facility still occupies space, contributes presence, and may be visited, but produces nothing. It can return online during a later adequately powered Production. A Facility may be built for two Runway on the acting piece’s non-Frontier hex if one of that hex’s two Facility spaces is free. Frontier has no Facility spaces. Rivals cannot destroy Facilities. Generator construction unlocks in Era II and requires the acting piece to be on an Energy hex. I may build only one ordinary Generator. Power Corridor builds an Emergency Power Complex for one Runway; Thermal or Water Basin builds a Civic Heat Battery for two. Each Energy hex has three shared Generator slots, separate from Facility spaces. Civic Heat Battery supplies three Power and grants one Trust when constructed. Emergency Power Complex supplies four Power and adds one Scrutiny during every Production. Every connected ordinary Generator with an eligible Facility operates automatically. Organize can recruit a Team at the acting piece’s destination for two Runway and then move one CEO or Team up to two extra steps; move CEOs/Teams for five total adjacent steps; or pay one Runway to move a Facility at the destination into an adjacent legal Facility space. A moved Facility carries its starting-grid state and contract/project tokens, but Power and contract activity are recalculated. Deploy requires Capability 2/4/6/8/10 for Customers 1–5. It normally costs one Compute, gains the next Customer, and adds one Scrutiny; Human Access District waives the Compute cost. Influence moves normally, then either uses an eligible political location for Trust/Scrutiny effects or creates/terminates a Joint Venture at one of my Facilities. Consensus Network removes two Scrutiny total; Civic Permission Authority grants two Trust total; Allocation Exchange grants the ordinary one Trust or removes one Scrutiny. Joint Ventures use available numbered matched pairs on two adjacent Facilities owned by different consenting players unless a faction rule changes range. Both hosts must be powered during Production. Each partner gains only the resource shown by the contract icon on the other host tile. A complete proposal names both hosts and the partner; rejection, silence, or pass consumes that Influence effect with no alternate proposal. Either partner may spend Influence solely to terminate one shared Joint Venture. Contracts remain owned but operate only while their fixed hosts qualify; tokens move with their hosts. Co-location means sharing a hex, while adjacency means host hexes share an edge. Consent is project-specific and grants no control or general trade right. Mega-Cluster unlocks in Era II, uses an available numbered pair across adjacent Facilities, costs three Runway and two Compute in total, adds two Scrutiny, and requires the acting piece to end on either host hex. Construction does not require prior Power. A solo project uses two of my Facilities, both locally eligible for my Power; when both hosts and two additional demand are powered, it produces three Compute. A joint project uses one locally powered host from each consenting player. The lead pays two Runway and one Compute, the partner one of each; each powers its own host plus one extra demand, producing two Compute to the lead and one to the partner. Rejection, pass, or silence consumes the Escalation. Hosts must stay adjacent. Reorganization occurs globally after normal movement: move every Team up to one hex, and optionally return one Team to supply to gain three Runway and add one Scrutiny. It neither resolves nor readies another Action. Open Weights occurs globally after movement: every player gains one Capability; I additionally gain two Trust and remove one of my Scrutiny. Narrative Capture occurs globally after movement and lets me remove two Scrutiny, gain two Runway, or give one Scrutiny to a player with more Customers than me. Agent Swarm requires two different unused Core Actions. Move once, resolve both from the same destination in either order, pay all costs, apply the visit bonus to only one, exhaust both, flip Agent Swarm, and add three Scrutiny. Declare AGI requires Capability 9+, at least three Customers, at least three existing Grid-Ready Facilities, Trust 2+, and spending three Compute. It occurs globally after normal movement, checks requirements on resolution, adds three Scrutiny, and scores seven Mandate for the first valid declaration or five for later ones. Play continues and AGI is not required to win. A Facility becomes Grid-Ready only after receiving its complete Facility demand during a completed Production. It immediately returns to normal if moved, if its legal connection is lost, or during a Production in which it lacks full Power. Building, moving, linking, or reconnecting after the latest Production requires a later successful Production before Grid-Ready status is earned or restored. A Facility built in Era IV cannot support an AGI declaration that Era. Fusion Demonstrator unlocks in Era IV. The acting piece must end on Power Corridor; pay five Runway, occupy one of its three Generator slots, gain six Power capacity, score two Mandate, and add three Scrutiny. Fusion counts as an owned Generator for local eligibility but not against the one-ordinary-Generator limit. It cannot be constructed if the three slots are full. At each Era’s start, advance the Era card, read New this Era, reveal one of its three Mandates and box the other two unseen, ready all six Core Actions, and award that Era’s Escalation availability. Once during my active resolution, immediately before or after Act, I may make one complete offer of Runway, Compute, and/or Safety to one rival. They accept, reject, or make one complete counteroffer; I then accept or reject. No redirection or further counteroffer is allowed. Accepted resources transfer immediately and remain subject to caps. Future promises are non-binding. Power purchases and persistent agreements use their own procedures. General discussion creates no game state. Missing responses are rejection/pass. Paced Play is optional only if agreed before play; timer expiry never creates consent. Production is resolved box-by-box for all players: Generate, Trade, Allocate, Produce, then Partner. Within a box, Initiative order applies unless specified otherwise; no player completes the whole sequence ahead of everyone else. Generate identifies local eligibility and automatically operates Generators with at least one eligible Facility; Emergency Power Complex adds one Scrutiny, and Headline generation is added. From Era III, during Trade, each player in Initiative order may request Power once from one adjacent rival connection. The supplier may accept or reject and may sell at most one Power that Production. Accepted Power costs one Runway per unit paid directly to the supplier. Only Generator or Fusion capacity may be sold; starting-grid and emergency Power cannot. Purchased Power lasts only that Production. During Allocate, combine legal starting-grid, Generator, purchased, and emergency capacity; assign it once among eligible Facilities and Mega-Clusters; flip fully powered Facilities Grid-Ready and all others normal. Produce powered Facilities first, then one Runway per Customer, then active Mega-Clusters. Partner then produces active Joint Ventures in ascending contract-number order. Apply resource caps after each Production gain. Each Era ends with Public Audit. Risky effects put my colored Scrutiny into the opaque bag. If all ten are already in the bag when another is required, immediately pay one Runway or lose one Trust, using the available option if only one exists; if neither is available, no further loss occurs. For a four-player game, draw 2/3/4/5 cubes in Eras I–IV. The table provides adjusted counts for 2, 3, 5, and 6 players using round(base × players ÷ 4), with halves upward and a minimum of one. In Eras I–III, each drawn player cube makes its owner pay one Runway or lose one Trust. In Era IV, it makes the owner pay an indivisible two Runway or lose one Mandate; with fewer than two Runway, lose Mandate if possible, and at zero Mandate reduce Runway to zero. Drawn player cubes return to their owners; undrawn cubes remain in the bag. A drawn black Systemic Risk cube applies the current Era penalty to every player with at least three Customers, then returns to supply. Consensus Network Facilities may remove cubes before the draw. Each revealed Era Mandate supplies its exact qualification and criterion. If nobody qualifies, nobody scores. Otherwise, the qualifying leader scores two Mandate; tied qualifying leaders each score one. Other resources, control, and public score do not break the tie. Fund gives either two Runway, or four Runway plus two Scrutiny. A Fund action at Allocation Exchange gains one additional Runway. Research costs one Compute and reveals Training cards one at a time. Each first ordinary domain—Code, Science, Web, Books, Images, Video, or Synthetic—adds one provisional Capability. After any non-duplicate card, stop and bank or continue. An unprotected duplicate loses all provisional Capability, adds one Scrutiny, and ends the run; prior Trust, Scrutiny, and Runway changes remain. All revealed cards are discarded afterward. On a duplicate, one Safety or a once-per-run Research Commons visit discards it and immediately banks, but never permits continuing. Curated Corpus becomes an unrevealed ordinary domain or duplicates if all seven are present. Benchmark Leak adds two provisional Capability and one Scrutiny but is not a domain. Licensed Dataset costs one Runway to continue; declining banks and ends. The first Synthetic Loop is the special Loop domain for one provisional Capability; another is a duplicate, and after the first Loop the next duplicate cannot be protected by Safety, Research Commons, or a faction ability. Human Evaluation grants one Trust, banks, and ends. At game end, read the twelve-Headline Future Timeline Era by Era, then lose one Mandate per offline Facility, resolve the shared World Ending, and only then announce the highest-Mandate institution. Mandate cannot fall below zero and there is no other endgame scoring. AGI emerges only if at least one declaring institution finishes at Capability 9+. The ending is Open only if final Collective Trust is at least Setup Collective Trust plus player count and unresolved black cubes in the bag are fewer than player count; otherwise it is Closed. AGI/Open gives The Singularity; AGI/Closed gives The Closed Loop; no AGI/Open gives The Plural Future; no AGI/Closed gives Assured Continuity. Highest Mandate wins. Ties break by Trust, then Customers, then Compute, then joint victory with an extremely serious merger announcement.
